# T6.2 (TASKS.md) -- DESIGN.md §3 degenerate-case table, row "Heir is
# log-behind at crash (lag bound was violated in flight)": the heir falls
# behind *after* being announced (the leader crashes before its next
# heartbeat tick ever re-runs selection and would have demoted it), so it
# still believes itself heir and campaigns first on the fast timeout -- but
# loses the vote on log-completeness, the same untouched safety check every
# vanilla candidate is subject to. A non-heir then times out and wins.
# Safety intact throughout: nothing here touches vote-granting rules.
#
# max-heir-lag=1 makes the lag bound trivial to violate with a couple of
# undelivered entries. min-heir-tenure=1 as in the other T6.2 files, so it
# doesn't interfere with anything being tested here.

log-level error
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=50 max-heir-lag=1 min-heir-tenure=1
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=255
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=100
----
ok

# The leader is deposed right here (never ticked again). 2 still believes

ok

# Only 2 and 3 -- 1 is gone. 2's MsgVote reaches 3, but 3's own log is

# 3 also saw 2's higher-term vote request, so it stepped down to that same
# term and, per T4.4, had its own heir belief cleared on that term bump --
# from here on 3 uses a vanilla timeout, not the backed-off one. Two full
# rounds guarantees crossing the vanilla range regardless of the random
# draw (same margin used in heir_dead_fallback.txt), without risking a
# second, spurious campaign.
tick-election 3
----
ok

----
ok

# 3 campaigns at the next term; 2 (still a stale candidate from its failed
# round) sees the higher term, steps down, and grants -- 3's log is at
# least as up to date as 2's own. Non-heir wins, vanilla-style, exactly one
# extra round after the heir's failed attempt.
